speaker: will_kemp
text: There. Ten days of Lent they got, and a new coat of paint out of it. We got our consciences.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A conscience needs no elm boards.

speaker: hired_men
text: It is the last. I came back from over the water. The players are stopped. Henslowe has carpenters and a painter in from Monday, to board the house and paint it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: I came up the street to hear that said in the air, and not only in a tavern.

speaker: hired_men
text: I counted what was lying there. Three hundred and twenty-five elm boards, on the Bankside, at twenty-four shillings, and lime-tubs beside them.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Twenty-four shillings, and a painter. They will come out of Lent newer than we shall.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Newer, and idle. So are we. Tomorrow the Queen pays. Today nobody plays.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: I was pleased, for as long as a man can be pleased at another house spending while it earns nothing. Then I remembered our own timber, and the pleasure went.

speaker: hired_men
text: No bill goes up beside the old one tomorrow. That title stays until the weather has it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the post tells the truth for a day. One title. After it, nothing.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And what did the house take? You were there.

speaker: hired_men
text: I was there to look at boards. I do not carry their purse home in my mouth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep it on their side of the river.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: If we are matching them, our pause spends too. The north side of our own house is not a rumour.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Honest is what we have, instead of a yard. It is a thin wage, Will.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is the wage we named on Ash Wednesday. I said we should all be equally idle. Here is the equality.

speaker: hired_men
text: The tubs I will swear to. The count of the boards I will swear to. Another man's book I will not.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Three hundred and twenty-five. A long face of boards, if they mean a wall.

speaker: hired_men
text: They mean to board and to paint. I saw the carpenter's chalk. I did not see a play.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Ten days. A coat of paint. And our hands kept off it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Clean hands do not hang a second bill. Leave the post.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Then we are matched. Idle, and idle. I dislike a match I cannot win.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Dislike it until tomorrow. The Queen's money is a different post.

speaker: will_kemp
text: If the bag is light I shall blame the paint.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Blame the fast. The paint is theirs.

speaker: hired_men
text: I have given you the boards and the shillings they stand at. Do not ask me for a total I did not add.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: No one here is adding it. Twenty-four shillings is the figure you brought. It can stay a figure.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Good. I am happier with a number I can see than with a number in a book across the water.
